proof:
# Arbitrarily many global maximizing integer bases at fixed integer dimension

For every integer s>=1 and every continuous dimension d>=1 there is
an actual convex body with n=2 whose mixed halfspace depth has at
least 2s+1 distinct globally maximizing integer bases. All these
maximizers have the same continuous coordinate. Thus no finite bound
depending only on n,d can count global maximizing bases in the class
of arbitrary faceted fibers. This is NOT an OC counterexample.

## 1. The three-row body

First let d=1 and use integer coordinates (p,q) and continuous x. Set

  r=4s+2,   R=7s+4,
  C_s={-1<=q<=1, |p|<=r-(r-s)q, |x|<=2+q}.

This is a compact full-dimensional convex polytope. Its integer rows
q=-1,0,1 have respective p-radii R,r,s and interval half-widths
1,2,3. In particular all its nonempty integer fibers have positive
length. Its total mixed mass is

  M_s=2(2R+1)+4(2r+1)+6(2s+1)=72s+44.                 (1)

Put T_s=24s+14. We prove that every point

  (j,0,0),   j=-s,...,s,                              (2)

has absolute halfspace depth T_s, which is the GLOBAL maximum.
No assertion that (2) lists every global maximizer is needed.

## 2. An exact four-cap global upper cover

The caps H_+={x+q>=0}, H_-={-x+q>=0} each have mass

  2(2r+1)+4(2s+1)=T_s.

They capture zero bottom-row length, half the middle row, and length
4 in each top fiber. Together they cover every point with q=0 or 1.
The caps G_+={x-3(q+1)>=0}, G_-={-x-3(q+1)>=0} isolate the bottom
row and each have mass 2R+1=14s+9<T_s. Together they cover that row.
The exclusions of the other rows are strict: 2-3<0 and 3-6<0.
Thus four actual closed caps cover the entire mixed set, proving
global absolute depth at most T_s.

## 3. An all-tilt lower bound at the outer anchor

Consider y=(s,0,0). By reflection in x and positive scaling every
nonvertical through-point cap is x+a(p-s)+bq>=0. Let

  F_s(a,b,c)=sum_(p,q) [w_q+a(p-s)+bq+c]_0^(2w_q),
  (w_-1,w_0,w_1)=(1,2,3).

We first use c=0. Reflection p->-p changes a negative tilt -a,
a>=0, into the positive-a margin plus 2as. Hence
F_s(-a,b,c)>=F_s(a,b,c), for every c, and a>=0 suffices.

The middle row has shifted indices k=p-s from -(5s+2) to 3s+2.
Pairing k with -k in the symmetric block yields the exact formula

  F_mid(a)=12s+10+sum_(K=3s+3)^(5s+2) (2-Ka)_+.

Consequently, for every a>=0,

  F_mid(a)>=16s+10-s(8s+5)a,
  F_mid(a)>=12s+10.                                   (3)

Here there are exactly 2s leftover terms, and their K sum is
s(8s+5). The first bound uses (2-Ka)_+>=2-Ka; no assumption on
which terms are positive has been made.

For the bottom row define B_a as the distribution of x+ak for
integer k=-8s-4,...,6s+4, each carrying unit density on [-1,1].
Let U_a be the distribution of x+aj for j=0,...,2s, each carrying
unit density on [-3,3]. The bottom captured mass is B_a([b,infinity));
the top captured mass is 6(2s+1)-U_a([b,infinity)). These are atomless
finite measures. The latter formula reflects the top continuous
coordinate and uses j=s-p.

Set L=4s+2. There is an explicit disjoint injection of ALL target
intervals into actual bottom intervals:

|target index j|target x-range|bottom index k|receiving x_s|
|--:|:--|:--|:--|
|0,...,2s|[-3,-1]|2j|x+2|
|0,...,2s|[-1,1]|2j+1|x|
|0,...,2s|[1,3]|j+L|x-2|

Every image is the whole interval [-1,1] of its labeled bottom
fiber. The first two rows use all distinct indices 0,...,4s+1;
the last uses 4s+2,...,6s+2. These indices lie in the actual bottom
range, so no receiving measure is counted twice. Each translation
preserves length and the three pieces partition each target source.

For the first row the change in projected scalar value is 2+ja>=0;
for the second it is (j+1)a>=0; for the last it is La-2. Thus at any
tail threshold t only the last pieces can lose captured mass, with
loss at most (2-La)_+ per unit-density piece. We have proved, for
ALL real t and a>=0,

  B_a([t,infinity))
    >=U_a([t,infinity))-(2s+1)(2-La)_+.                 (4)

This is a concrete transport inequality between actual row sources,
not a claim of concavity or a statement about selected tilt minima.

The endpoint captured mass is therefore at least

  6(2s+1)-(2s+1)(2-La)_+.                              (5)

For 0<=a<=2/L, add the first bound of (3) to (5). The result is

  F_s(a,b,0)>=T_s+[(2s+1)L-s(8s+5)]a
             =T_s+(3s+2)a>=T_s.                       (6)

For a>=2/L, use the second bound of (3) instead:

  F_s(a,b,0)>=12s+10+12s+6=T_s+2>T_s.                 (7)

These hold for EVERY real b. At a=0,b=1 equality T_s is attained
by H_+, so the lower bound is exact.

Containing caps can be moved through the anchor. A vertical through-
point cap is the limit of caps with margin x+t A.(p-s,q), as t tends
to infinity. Strict-sign fibers tend to full or empty; zero-sign
fibers contribute half their intervals, hence no more than the full
boundary mass of the CLOSED vertical cap. Since every finite-t mass
is at least T_s, the original vertical cap also has mass at least
T_s. This proves the all-ambient-halfspace lower bound at y.

Reflection in p proves it at (-s,0,0). Every point in (2) is a
convex combination of these endpoints and belongs to S. Quasiconcavity
of halfspace depth gives its lower bound T_s, and the cover in
Section 2 gives the matching global upper bound.

## 4. Paired thresholds and every continuous dimension

The same exact source satisfies, for all real a,b,c,

  F_s(a,b,c)+F_s(a,b,-c)>=2T_s.                         (8)

Again reflect p to take a>=0. The endpoint contribution to F_s(a,b,c)
is B_a([b-c,infinity))+6(2s+1)-U_a([b+c,infinity)). After adding the
-c expression, apply (4) at b-c and b+c. The U tails cancel, leaving
the paired endpoint lower bound twice (5).

In the middle row, the symmetric block k=-(3s+2),...,3s+2 contributes
twice 12s+10 to the c,-c pair. For each remaining -K,

  [2-Ka+c]_0^4+[2-Ka-c]_0^4>=2(2-Ka)_+.

To verify this, put v=2-Ka<=2. For v<=0 the claim is immediate.
For 0<v<=2 take c>=0 by symmetry. If c<=v the sum is 2v; if c>v
the sum is min(v+c,4)>=2v. Therefore paired middle mass is at least
2F_mid(a). Equations (6)-(7) prove (8).

Now let d>=2 and let Q be any centrally symmetric convex body in
R^(d-1), centered at zero. Use C_s x Q with continuous coordinates
(x,w). A through-(s,0;0,0) cap with nonzero x coefficient can be
normalized to x+a(p-s)+bq+v.w>=0, after reflection in x if necessary.
Its mixed mass is int_Q F_s(a,b,v.w)dw. Symmetry Q=-Q and (8) give

  int_Q F_s(a,b,v.w)dw>=T_s |Q|.

When the x coefficient is zero, add epsilon x to its margin. These
perturbed caps still pass through the anchor and have the bound just
proved. Off the unperturbed boundary their indicators converge; on
that boundary their limiting upper indicators are at most the
indicator of the CLOSED original cap. The finite source and bounded
convergence give original mass at least the limiting upper mass,
hence at least T_s |Q|. Thus all closed ambient halfspaces are covered,
including vertical ones with positive boundary mass.

The four-cap global upper cover extends with zero w coefficients,
so every point (j,0;0,0), j=-s,...,s, is a GLOBAL maximizer with

  depth = T_s/M_s = (24s+14)/(72s+44)
                  =1/3-2/[3(72s+44)].                  (9)

The d=1 proof is the zero-dimensional-factor case. Taking s arbitrarily
large proves the unbounded-count assertion at fixed n=2 and every
fixed d>=1. Each value in (9) exceeds 1/8 and therefore exceeds the
OC target gamma_d/4. The example refutes a counting restriction, not
the required sharp lower bound. Its supporting facets also preserve
the applicability boundary of the facet-free strict-interpolation
theorem.
